message.content:
**Answer:**  
It would take roughly **six months** to paint the entire Eiffel Tower.

---

### Why six months?

| Step | What’s involved | Time per step | Notes |
|------|-----------------|---------------|-------|
| **Surface prep** | Cleaning, rust removal, sandblasting | 2–3 weeks | The tower’s iron is exposed to the elements; it needs to be cleaned before paint can adhere. |
| **Primer coat** | Application of a corrosion‑blocking primer | 2–3 weeks | Primer protects the metal and improves paint adhesion. |
| **Base coat** | First layer of protective paint (often a light gray or “Eiffel Tower” color) | 2–3 weeks | Provides the main protective layer. |
| **Topcoat** | Final decorative coat (usually a darker shade or a special finish) | 2–3 weeks | Gives the tower its signature look. |
| **Drying & curing** | Allow paint to cure between coats and after final coat | 1–2 weeks | Paint must dry fully to avoid peeling. |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | Inspect for missed spots, re‑paint as needed | 1–2 weeks | Ensures uniform coverage and quality. |

**Total:** 10–12 weeks ≈ 2–3 months for the actual painting work, plus additional time for logistics, safety checks, and crew rotation. In practice, the entire project—including planning, permits, crew scheduling, and post‑painting inspections—spans about **six months**.

---

### How this compares to other large‑scale paint jobs

| Structure | Surface area (m²) | Paint job duration | Comments |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------------|----------|
| Eiffel Tower | ~10,000 | 6 months | 5,000 tons of iron, 18,000 rivets. |
| Burj Khalifa | ~200,000 | 1 year | 828 m tall, 160 000 m² of glass/steel. |
| Statue of Liberty | ~5,000 | 3 months | 46 m tall, copper cladding. |

The Eiffel Tower’s painting cycle is typically every **7 years**, so the maintenance schedule is well established and the six‑month window is standard.

---

### Bottom line

If you’re planning a paint‑job for a landmark like the Eiffel Tower, expect a **half‑year project** from start to finish. This includes prep, multiple coats, drying, inspections, and crew rotations—all coordinated to keep the tower safe and operational during the work.
